

**Amazon Review Analytics Using PySpark & NLP**

**Godwin Gyamfi Duah**

Harrisburg University of Science & Technology

2nd April, 2026

**Overview**

This project analyzes Amazon Electronics product reviews using PySpark for distributed data processing and VADER (NLTK) for NLP-based sentiment classification. The analysis covers rating distributions, review trends over time, top-reviewed products, and a comparison of textual sentiment against numerical star ratings. Key findings confirm a strong skew toward positive reviews, a significant growth in review volume in recent years, and high alignment between VADER sentiment labels and star ratings.

**Objectives**

* Analyze customer rating distributions and trends

* Identify how review activity changes over time

* Identify the most frequently reviewed products

* Perform sentiment analysis on review text

* Compare NLP-derived sentiment against numerical star ratings

**Dataset**

The dataset used in this project is the Amazon Review Dataset provided by Julian McAuley:

[https://nijianmo.github.io/amazon/index.html](https://nijianmo.github.io/amazon/index.html) 

Each record of the Amazon Electronics product reviews includes:

| Field | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| asin | Product ID |
| reviewerID | Unique reviewer identifier |
| overall | Star rating (1-5) |
| reviewText | Full text of the review |
| reviewTime | Date the review was submitted |

**Data Pipeline**

Raw JSON (Google Drive)

              ⇓

  Load with PySpark

              ⇓

  Extract & Clean Fields

  (cast types, parse dates, drop duplicates)

              ⇓

  Feature Engineering

  (review\_year, review\_month, review\_length)

              ⇓

  Save as Parquet  ⇒  Reload for Analysis

               ⇓

  Spark SQL Analytics

               ⇓

  VADER Sentiment (1% sample)

               ⇓

  Matplotlib Visualizations

**Key Features**

**1\. Data Engineering**

* Processed large-scale JSON data using PySpark  
* Converted raw data into structured format  
* Removed duplicates and handled missing values  
* Created new features such as: ‘**review\_year\`,  \`review\_month\`, \`review\_length\`**

**2\. SQL-Based Analytics**

* Rating distribution analysis  
* Review trends over time  
* Average rating progression  
* Identification of top reviewed products

**3\. Review Behavior Analysis**

* Compared review length across rating levels  
* Found that lower-rated reviews tend to be longer and more detailed

**4\. Sentiment Analysis (NLP)**

* Applied VADER sentiment analysis to review text  
* Classified reviews as Positive, Neutral, or Negative  
* Compared sentiment labels against numerical star ratings


**Key Insights**

* Review activity increased significantly over time, peaking between 2014–2016  
* Average product ratings improved over time, indicating increased customer satisfaction  
* Negative reviews tend to be longer than positive ones  
* Sentiment and numerical ratings do not always align, highlighting the value of text-based analysis

**Analysis & Results**

**Rating Distribution**  
Reviews were grouped by star rating (1–5) and expressed as a percentage of total volume to show the overall distribution of customer satisfaction   
![][image1]  
The majority of reviews are concentrated at the 5-star rating, indicating a strong positive bias in the dataset. Ratings 1 and 2 account for a much smaller share, suggesting most customers who leave reviews are satisfied with their purchase.

**Review Volume Over Time**  
Review volume was aggregated by year and expressed as a percentage of total reviews to reveal growth trends in customer engagement over time.

![][image2]

Review activity grew substantially in later years, particularly from 2013, reflecting the broader rise of e-commerce and online review culture.

**Top Reviewed Products**

**Sentiment vs Star Rating**

VADER sentiment analysis was applied to a 1% sample of reviews, classifying each as positive, neutral, or negative. These labels were then compared against numerical star ratings.

![][image3]

NLP sentiment labels align strongly with star ratings, positive sentiment dominates at ratings 4 and 5, while negative sentiment is most prevalent at ratings 1 and 2\. The neutral category is distributed more evenly, likely capturing short or ambiguous review text that VADER cannot classify with confidence.

**How To Run**

**Prerequisites**

* A Google account with Google Drive access  
* The Amazon Electronics dataset (Electronics\_5.json), download from [here](https://nijianmo.github.io/amazon/index.html). 

**Steps**

* Upload the dataset to your Google Drive at the following path: MyDrive/DATA\_ANALYTICS\_PROJECT/data/Electronics\_5.json  
* Open Amazon\_Review\_Analytics.ipynb in Google Colab  
* Run the first cell to mount your Google Drive — you will be prompted to sign in and grant access  
* Run all remaining cells in order from top to bottom  
  The following dependencies are installed automatically inside the notebook:

 ***pip install pyspark nltk***

* The cleaned dataset will be saved automatically as a Parquet file at: MyDrive/DATA\_ANALYTICS\_PROJECT/data/clean\_reviews.parquet

This speeds up any future reruns, you won't need to reprocess the raw JSON again.

**Conclusion**

This project demonstrates an end-to-end data analytics pipeline, from raw JSON ingestion and distributed processing with PySpark, through SQL-based aggregation, to NLP-driven sentiment analysis and visual reporting. The results validate that customer-assigned star ratings and NLP-derived sentiment are highly consistent, making either a reliable proxy for measuring satisfaction at scale.

Potential next steps include:

* Building an interactive dashboard using Power BI  
* Extending sentiment analysis using machine learning models  
* Performing product-level deep analysis  
* Detecting fake or biased reviews
